MINUTES
  MALIBU ARTS COMMISSION
  REGULAR MEETING
  OCTOBER 25, 2022
  TELECONFERENCED - VARIO US LOCATIONS
  9:00A.M.

The following meeting was held pursuant to AB 361 and fully teleconferenced from various
locations during the coronavirus disease (COVID-19) pandemic.

MEETING CALL TO ORDER

  Chair Cherin called the meeting to order at 9:06 a.m.

ROLL CALL

  The following persons were recorded in attendance via teleconference by the Recording
  Secretary:

  PRESENT: Chair Lotte Cherin; Vice Chair Fireball Lawrence; and Commissioners Barry
  Haldeman, Julia Holland, and Peter Jones

  ABSENT: Ex-Officio Graeme Clifford

  ALSO PRESENT: Jesse Bobbett, Community Services Director; Kristin Riesgo,
  Community Services Deputy Director; and Brittany Saleaumua, Administrative Assistant

PLEDGE OF ALLEGIANCE

  Community Services Director Bobbett led the Pledge of Allegiance.

CITY OF MALIBU VISION STATEMENT

  Commissioner Jones read the City of Malibu Vision Statement.

APPROVAL OF AGENDA

  Chair Cherin requested to move Item No. 4.B. after Item No. 2.A.

MOTION  Chair Cherin moved, and Commissioner Haldeman seconded a motion to approve
  the agenda hearing Item No. 4.B. after Item No. 2.A. The question was called, and
  the motion carried unanimously.

REPORT ON POSTING OF AGENDA

  Administrative Assistant Saleaumua reported the agenda for the meeting was properly
  posted on October 21, 2022.

ITEMl  CEREMONIAL/PRESENTATIONS

  None.

ITEM 2.A.  PUBLIC COMMENTS

  None.

ITEM4  OLD BUSINESS

  B.  Solstice Canyon Creek Beautification Project
  Recommended Action: 1) Review the artist recommendation from the Solstice
  Canyon Creek Beautification Project Ad Hoc Committee; and 2) Provide an artist
  recommendation for City Council approval.

  Community Services Deputy Director Riesgo presented the staff report.

  In response to Chair Cherin, Community Services Director Bobbett stated staff
  would complete the Ca!Trans agreements once an artist was approved for the
  project. He stated CalTrans had requested the City maintain the artwork, but the
  City has objected since the artwork is located on CalTrans property.

  In response to Commissioner Haldeman, Community Services Director Bobbett
  stated the artwork must be completed by June 2023.

  In response to Chair Cherin, Community Services Deputy Director Riesgo stated
  staff would work with Cal Trans regarding the artist payment.

  Matt Doolin thanked the Commission for the opportunity to submit a proposal and
  stated his proposal could evolve based on Commission feedback.

  Vice Chair Lawrence thanked Mr. Doolin for his proposal. He stated the Solstice
  Canyon Creek Beautification Project ad hoc recommended muralist Jules Muck.
  He stated Ms. Muck would create ten oversized canvas pieces at half scale, which
  would be used to promote the project, and the final piece would be completed by
  June 2023.

  Commissioner Jones stated CalTrans would not accept artwork with text, which
  eliminated one proposal, and sculpture proposals were also eliminated.

  Vice Chair Lawrence stated CalTrans would allow three installment payments for
  the artist. He stated the artist would purchase materials and supplies with the first
  payment.

  In response to Chair Cherin, Vice Chair Lawrence stated he viewed all social media
  platforms from the artists that submitted proposals, but he did not personally contact
   Malibu Arts Commission Regular Meeting
  Minutes of October 25, 2022
  Page 3 of6

  each artist. He stated Ms. Muck had a social media following, which was an aspect
  the Commission should consider.

  Commissioner Jones stated it was important to have diversity and select an artist
  that had not worked on a Malibu public art project.

  In response to Commissioner Haldeman, Vice Chair Lawrence stated Ms. Muck
  would create the mural on a mounted surface and attach it to the tunnel. He stated
  the ad hoc committee selected Ms. Muck for her street art painting style and her
  connection to young artists through her social media platforms.

  Commissioner Haldeman indicated agreement with the ad hoc committee's
  recommendation. He stated young artists would relate to the artwork.

  Chair Cherin indicated disagreement with the ad hoc committee's recommendation
  to select Ms. Muck. She stated she preferred artist Eugene Daub because his
  proposal was thorough and showcased the history of Solstice Canyon.

MOTION  Vice Chair Lawrence moved, and Commissioner Haldeman seconded a motion to
  recommend Jules Muck as the recommended artist for City Council approval. The
  question was called, and the motion carried 4-1, Chair Cherin dissenting.

  In response to Commissioner Haldeman, Commissioner Jones stated the artwork
  would be located on one side of the tunnel.

ITEM 2.B.  COMMISSION AD HOC COMMITTEE REPORTS

  I.  Arts in Education

  Community Services Deputy Director Riesgo stated poetry workshops were
  planned at Malibu High School, Malibu Elementary School, and Webster
  Elementary School. She stated poetry workshops had occurred at Malibu
  Middle School and Distance Learning classes.

  2.  Malibu Public Art Exhibitions

  Commissioner Holland stated the art exhibition featuring S. Heather
  Edwards would end on November 10, 2022, and the Call for Artist for Music
  Inspired Art was open through November 6, 2022.

  3.  Business and Community Outreach

  Commissioner Haldeman stated he worked with the Malibu Chamber of
  Commerce on the Art Share program and the organization was planning an
  evening event for businesses to be open late and artists to display their
  artwork.

  4.  Social Media

  Vice Chair Lawrence stated S. Heather Edwards has sold five pieces of
  artwork since exhibiting in the Malibu City Gallery. He stated Ms. Edwards
  has promoted the gallery on social media.

  In response to Commissioner Haldeman, Community Services Director
  Bobbett stated the Commission would continue to meet until new
  Commissioners were appointed by the new City Council.

  5.  Solstice Canyon Creek Beautification Project

  Updates were provided under Item No. 4.B.

ITEM3  CONSENT CALENDAR

MOTION  Chair Cherin moved, and Commissioner Jones seconded a motion to approve the
  Consent Calendar. The question was called, and the motion carried unanimously.

  The Consent Calendar consisted of the following items:

  A.  Previously Discussed Items
  None.
  B.  New Items
  1.  Approval of Minutes
  Recommended Action: Approve the minutes for the September 27, 2022
  Malibu Arts Commission Regular meeting.

ITEM4  OLD BUSINESS (Continued)

  A.  Malibu Arts Center
  Recommended Action: Discuss ideas for an arts center in Malibu.

  Community Services Director Bobbett presented the staff report.

  In response to Chair Cherin, Administrative Assistant Saleaumua stated the survey
  questions submitted by Commissioners were included as Attachment 1.

  Commissioner Jones requested staff send an email with the Agenda and a separate
  email with survey questions.

  In response to Commissioner Haldeman, Community Services Director Bobbett
  stated the survey would provide the Commission with community feedback
  regarding an arts center. He stated the survey results could be used to draft a
   Malibu Arts Commission Regular Meeting

  Commission recommendation to City Council when they discuss a plan for the
  vacant properties.
  ~

  Commissioner Holland stated she would consolidate the Commissioner's survey
  questions and provide a draft survey for the Commission to review.

  In response to Vice Chair Lawrence, Commissioner Holland stated she would draft
  the survey before the November 22, 2022 Regular meeting.

  Commissioner Jones requested staff email the draft survey before the November
  22, 2022 Regular meeting to allow the Commission time to review the questions.

ITEMS  NEW BUSINESS

  None.

ITEM6  STAFF UPDATES

  Community Services Deputy Director Riesgo provided an update on Poet Laureate
  programs and upcoming commission meetings.

CONSENSUS By Consensus, the Commission agreed to hold a Special meeting on December 21,
  2022 at 9:00 AM and cancel the December 27, 2022 Regular meeting.

  Community Services Director Bobbett provided an update on department staff
  changes.

ITEM7  COMMISSIONER REPORTS, COMMENTS AND INQUIRIES

  Commissioner Jones stated he was working on a book detailing his wife's treatment
  and recovery from multiple myeloma.

  Vice Chair Lawrence stated he released a Hilton Hotels Worldwide coloring book.
  He stated he celebrated I 0,000 episodes on his YouTube channel.

  Commissioner Holland stated she was working on a voiceover project and
  preparing for a holiday production at Malibu Elementary School.

  Commissioner Haldeman stated he recently visited the Amazonia photography
  exhibition by Sebastiao Salgado at the California Science Center and recommended
  the Commission view the exhibition.

  Chair Cherin stated she attended Malika Wilbur's keynote speech and residency
  exhibition, Project 562: Changing The Way We See Native America, at Santa
  Monica College.
